overview.description: Big Three (大三, Da San) is a strategic Chinese climbing game for 3 players from the Shaanxi province. It is closely related to games like 'Wa Keng' (Digging the Pit). In each deal, the 3s are the highest-ranking cards, and players bid in an auction to become the 'Declarer' who plays alone against the other two. The game is known for its peculiar ranking (3s high, 2s second) and the restriction that 3s, 2s, and Aces cannot be used in sequences.

history.origins: Originating in Shaanxi province, China, as a variation of the broader 'climbing' genre. It specifically targets three-player dynamics, making it a faster and more aggressive alternative to the four-player 'Tractor' family.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Developed as a regional folk game in Northern China.
1990s: Popularized in regional tournaments and under the name 'Wa Keng'.
Present: A staple of Chinese online gaming platforms and social clubs.
history.evolution: The game shifted from a simple shedding race to an auction-based format where the declarer takes a small widow, adding a tactical 'risk vs reward' phase before play.
history.cultural: Reflects the northern Chinese preference for three-player games, emphasizing individual skill and psychological bidding.

setup.dealing: The deck is dealt as follows: 16 cards to each player and 4 cards face down in the center (The Widow).

rules.objective: Be the first to shed all cards from your hand. If the declarer wins, they win points from both opponents; if the opponents win, the declarer pays both.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Auction**: Players bid 1, 2, or 3 points to take the contract. Highest bidder is Declarer. 2. **Widow**: Declarer takes the 4 cards from the widow into their hand. 3. **Climbing**: Players must play a combination of the same type but higher rank than the previous. 4. **Ranks**: 3 (High) > 2 > A > K > Q ... > 4 (Low). 5. **Combinations**: Singles, Pairs, Triples, and Sequences.
keyRules: 3s, 2s, and Aces cannot be part of a sequence (e.g., Q-K-A is illegal).
A Triple of 3s is an invincible 'Bomb' in some variations.
Players can pass on any turn, even if they can beat the current combo.

strategy.basic: Don't overbid for the Declarer role unless you hold at least one 3 and several 2s. The widow is small and rarely fixes a terrible hand.
strategy.intermediate: Counting the 3s: There are only four 3s in the deck. If you hold three of them, you control the game. Force opponents to waste their 3s on single cards.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Lead: As an opponent, lead a combo type the Declarer is likely weak in. If they passed on a pair earlier, keep leading pairs to prevent them from shedding their singles.
tips: Save your 3s to regain the lead when you have a long sequence to dump.
If you are an opponent, communicate through your plays—don't trap your partner!

list.name: Wa Keng (Digging the Pit)
list.description: Essentially the same game, but with different scoring multipliers for specific 'bombs'.
list.emptyOverridesReason: No separate engine configuration is needed; Wa Keng uses the same structure and only tweaks scoring multipliers outside the core blueprint.

difficulty.easy: Bids 3 points on any hand with an Ace. Plays lowest legal combo.
difficulty.medium: Evaluates hand strength for bidding. Tracks the four 3s. Prioritizes shedding large sets.
difficulty.hard: Optimal bidding model. Deduces Declarer's hand based on their bidding level and the widow cards. Coordinates perfectly with the other opponent.

considerations: Must implement the 'No A-2-3 in sequences' constraint.
Bidding logic requires a probability model for the 4-card widow.

ante.reason: Big Three is a point-based climbing game where stakes are determined by the auction rather than antes.

deal.reason: The initial distribution of sixteen cards per player and the four-card widow is handled by the system dealer.

reveal_market.reason: There is no shared community market in Big Three; only the widow exists which is taken by the declarer.

buy_market.reason: Players cannot purchase cards from a market; the widow is awarded to the highest bidder for free.

buy_stock.reason: There is no remaining stock to draw from during play; every card is in a hand or the widow at the start.

fold.reason: Players must remain in the game until someone sheds their entire hand to determine the round score.

check.reason: The game uses a climbing and passing structure rather than a vying structure with checks and bets.

call.reason: There is no pot to match in this game; competition is based on card ranking and bidding levels.

bet.reason: Success is measured by points won or lost from other players based on the auction result.

raise.reason: The auction allows for bidding escalation, but there are no wagering rounds during the actual play of cards.

declare.reason: Declarations are handled through the auction and combo play rather than a separate declaration phase.

reveal_hand.reason: Hands remain private until individual cards are played into climbing combos; no showdown occurs.

award_pot.reason: Points are transferred between players at the end of the round; there is no physical pot to award.

play_card.description: Play a valid combination (single, pair, triple, etc.) to beat the previous play.
play_card.constraints: Must match the combination type and exceed the previous rank.

draw.reason: Players receive their massive hands at the start and no further drawing occurs during the play phase.

discard.reason: Every card must be shed through valid climbing combinations; there is no separate discard or waste pile.

pass.description: Decline to play on the current trick cycle.
pass.constraints: May choose to pass even if a legal move is available.

bid.description: Bid for the Declarer role by offering points (1, 2, or 3).
bid.constraints: Must be higher than the previous bid.

meld.reason: Big Three is a climbing game based on beating combos rather than forming table melds.

go_out.reason: A player wins the round automatically upon playing their final card from hand.

notApplicableReasons.drawConfig: The full hand is dealt initially; no draw pile exists during the climbing phase.
notApplicableReasons.discardConfig: Cards are played to the table center or held; no separate discard pile is utilized.
notApplicableReasons.specialCards: Threes are high-ranking but do not trigger secondary automated engine effects.
notApplicableReasons.declarationMechanism: The auction result defines roles; no hidden declaration tokens are required.
notApplicableReasons.fishingConfig: Big Three is a climbing game and does not use a capture-from-tableau fishing mechanic.

shedding.burnRules: Round ends when two players pass consecutively.

customActions.description: Distribute sixteen cards to each player and set aside a four-card widow.
Offer a point value to take the contract.
Play a single, pair, triple, or sequence higher than the previous play.
High bidder reveals and takes the four-card widow into their hand.
Transfer points between players based on auction value and finishing order.

engine.handRankingSystem: None; rank hierarchy (3 > 2 > A > K...) determines combination strength.
engine.deckDescription: One standard 52-card deck consisting of four suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs), each with thirteen ranks. No jokers; used for Big Three (Chinese climbing game) where the three is the highest rank and players shed combinations in ascending order.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs). Suits do not break ties in Big Three; only the rank of the combination matters. Players play singles, pairs, triples, or sequences; the same rank in different suits is equal.
engine.rankDescription: Thirteen ranks per suit in Big Three order: three (highest), two, ace, king, queen, jack, ten, nine, eight, seven, six, five, four (lowest). Combinations are played in ascending rank order; bombs may beat lower combinations.
engine.dealPattern: Cards are dealt individually to players and the widow.

hero.title: BIG THREE
hero.subtitle: Shaanxi Climbing
hero.tagline: The 3 is King. The Pit is deep. Empty your hand first.

synthesis.shortDescription: A fierce three-player climbing game from Northern China. Bid for the privilege of taking the 'Widow' and playing solo against your rivals. With 3s at the top of the hierarchy and strict sequence rules, Big Three is a masterclass in hand management and tactical passing.

prompts.human: You have three 3s and two 2s. The bid is currently at '2 points'. With your hand and the four extra cards in the widow, can you beat two opponents combined? Bid '3 points' and take the lead!
prompts.ai: Game: Big Three (Da San). Type: Auction Climbing. Rules: 3 players. 16 cards each + 4 widow. Rank: 3>2>A>K...4. Restriction: 3, 2, A cannot be in sequences.

scoring.description: Points are awarded based on the bid level. Declarer wins bid amount from each opponent (x2) or loses it to each.
scoring.winCondition: Highest point total after a set session or reaching a target score.

penalties.Blocked: Failing to play any card after the declarer wins results in doubled penalties.

scoring.splitRules: None; only one player can be the first to empty their hand.

nullReasons.targetScore: Pagat describes per-hand win/loss units but no fixed session goal; this JSON uses 150 points as a conventional target that tables may adjust.
nullReasons.cardValues: Card values follow the Big Three rank hierarchy (3, 2, A, K ... 4) and are used for comparing combinations rather than accumulating per-card points.

assumptions: Selected a 150-point targetScore as a conventional session goal for Big Three since Pagat specifies only per-hand payments, not a fixed session length.
Encoded scoring.cardValues as numeric weights that match the described Big Three rank order (3 high, 4 low) to support engine comparisons.
